title: Hierarchical Architecture and Its Failure Mode

questions.question: A lead splits a product review between an engineering group and a legal group, then combines their summaries into one decision. Why is this grouping useful compared to sending every individual note straight to the lead?
options: Each group condenses its own findings, so the lead reads a few summaries instead of every raw note.
It guarantees that no group can ever make a mistake in its summary.
It removes the need for anyone to write down what they checked.
It lets the lead skip reading all summaries and guess the final answer.
questions.explanation: Seeing how grouped summaries reduce the load on one coordinator prepares you for this lesson, which implements that hierarchy and shows how a mislabeled request can slip through.

questions.question: Which branch labels does the happy-path call use?
options: ["engineering", "finance"]
["engineering", "legal"]
["legal", "finance"]
["engineering", "engineering"]
questions.explanation: `main` calls `top.run(task, branch_labels=["engineering", "legal"])`, so engineering and legal summaries reach the top on the happy path.

questions.question: What does the perturbed call `branch_labels=["engineering", "finance"]` demonstrate?
options: The finance worker refuses to answer because it is not in the hierarchy.
The legal sub-manager silently changes its own label to finance.
Finance answers its own review while the requested legal branch is missing.
The top manager reroutes the legal question to the lawyer automatically.
questions.explanation: `TopManager.run` accepts the supplied label and invokes `finance-manager`; it records `MISSING[legal]` only when a requested label is absent, so the legal review is not produced.

questions.question: What answer does the finance leaf return for the matched `finance` question?
options: React component audited; 2 issues.
Contract clauses A and B are non-compliant.
API endpoints audited; 1 issue.
Projected cost $42k/month; exceeds budget by 12%.
questions.explanation: The finance worker's canned dictionary maps `finance` to the projected $42k/month cost and 12% budget overrun.

questions.question: Why does the hierarchy scale summaries better than exposing every leaf to the top manager?
options: Each sub-manager aggregates its leaves, so the top receives branch summaries instead of every raw worker output.
Leaf workers never run; only the top manager writes summaries.
The top manager receives no branch information and guesses the answer.
The hierarchy encrypts all leaf outputs and therefore needs fewer tokens.
questions.explanation: `SubManager.run` creates a `SubSummary` from its leaves. `TopManager` synthesizes those summaries, reducing the top-level view while preserving local detail.

questions.question: What is the main failure mode shown when the top manager mislabels `legal` as `finance`?
options: A leaf raises a Python exception before it can answer.
The wrong branch can produce a plausible summary, so the error remains hidden until top-level synthesis.
The system automatically detects the semantic mismatch and retries legal.
All branches stop because one label is invalid.
questions.explanation: The finance branch dutifully returns a valid-looking finance answer. Nothing in the runtime validates that it answers the requested legal concern, so the decomposition error surfaces late.
